security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, example.com URLs, and the standard /.well-known/agent.json discovery path. The real concern is the Python server example binding to 0.0.0.0 without local authentication context. Copying it directly could expose an A2A endpoint.

remediation.issue: The Python server example binds to all network interfaces without showing authentication in the setup.
remediation.suggestion: Use 127.0.0.1 for local examples and add an authenticated deployment example before using 0.0.0.0.

remediation.issue: SDK install commands do not pin package versions, while the protocol is still evolving.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a2a-sdk and @a2a-js/sdk versions in setup commands or explain how users should choose current versions.

content.value_statement: Teams need a practical path to connect agents across frameworks. This skill guides A2A servers, clients, Agent Cards, streaming, and orchestration.
actual_capabilities: Outline A2A core concepts, including Agent Cards, tasks, messages, and artifacts.
Provide Python examples for A2A server setup, task execution, streaming, and cancellation.
Provide Python client examples for Agent Card discovery and message sending.
Provide Node.js examples for A2A server and client setup.
Show sequential and parallel orchestration patterns for multiple A2A agents.
Compare A2A and MCP so users choose the right integration pattern.
limitations: Examples are implementation templates, not complete production services.
Users must add real business logic, authentication, authorization, and monitoring.
The skill does not verify live endpoint behavior or SDK compatibility.
A2A is evolving, so users should confirm current protocol and SDK versions.

use_cases.title: Create an Agent Service
use_cases.description: Build a focused A2A server with an Agent Card, task handler, streaming updates, and cancellation support.

use_cases.title: Connect Existing Agents
use_cases.description: Add A2A clients that discover remote Agent Cards and send tasks to agents built on different frameworks.

use_cases.title: Plan Multi-Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Design routing, sequential delegation, and parallel fan-out across specialized agents while preserving task context.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a simple A2A server for a research assistant. Include the Agent Card, one skill, task handling, and cancellation.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an A2A client that discovers a remote Agent Card, sends a user task, and reports the returned task status.

prompt_templates.title: Support Streaming Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend the A2A implementation with streaming status updates, input-required handling, cancellation, and clear error states.

prompt_templates.title: Design Agent Orchestration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A2A orchestrator that routes tasks across research, writing, and review agents with retries and human handoff.

output_examples.input: Build an A2A support router for billing, technical, and sales questions.
output_examples.output: A plan for one router agent, three downstream agents, task routing rules, response aggregation, and human handoff.

output_examples.input: Create a client that sends a code review task to a remote A2A agent.
output_examples.output: A client flow that discovers the Agent Card, sends the review request, streams progress, and reports final status.

output_examples.input: Compare A2A with MCP for a new agent platform.
output_examples.output: A concise decision guide explaining when to use agent-to-agent communication and when to call tools through MCP.

best_practices: Keep each A2A agent focused on one capability domain.
Declare authentication, supported modalities, and skills clearly in the Agent Card.
Use streaming, cancellation, and input-required states for long-running tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not expose an A2A server publicly without authentication and authorization.
Do not create broad agents with vague skills that other agents cannot evaluate.
Do not use A2A when a simple tool call through MCP is enough.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build A2A servers, clients, Agent Cards, streaming flows, and multi-agent orchestration patterns.

faq.question: Does it support Python and Node.js?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes Python and Node.js examples for A2A server and client implementation.

faq.question: Does it create production-ready services?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance, but users must add security, deployment, testing, and monitoring.

faq.question: How is A2A different from MCP?
faq.answer: A2A connects agents to agents. MCP connects an agent to tools, data sources, or APIs.

faq.question: Can it help with agent discovery?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Agent Cards and the standard discovery endpoint used by A2A clients.

faq.question: Should I pin SDK versions?
faq.answer: Yes. The protocol is evolving, so pin versions and verify current documentation before deployment.
